newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Far East Gold - Eye on dollar/yen, producer hedges.
newsitem.headline: Far East Gold - Eye on dollar/yen, producer hedges.

text.p: Bullion dealers in Hong Kong and Singapore said on Friday they were watching the dollar/yen and the Australian dollar for further clues to gold's direction.
"The market rallied strongly in Asia and New York yesterday as the dollar weakened," said Jonathan Spall, Asia head of precious metals at Deutsche Bank AG's Hong Kong branch.
"People expected to see fresh buying from the Japanese today, and the market was left a little long," he said.
Hong Kong bullion was trading at $378.50/379.00 per ounce at 1100 (0300 GMT), down from New York's Thursday close at $378.75/379.25
Gold traders said Friday morning trade had been relatively quiet but that Australian producer selling had pushed gold down, absorbing Japanese buying.
Bullion traders in Japan arbitrage the gold market on dollar/yen swings, Hong Kong traders said, but noted that most arbitraging had been done on Thursday.
Japanese traders said Japanese trade houses are unlikely to buy gold actively in the near future, as uncertainty over the currency market could sideline Japanese private investors.
"Although some buying by trade houses in arbitrage trade was detected today, the buying interest is likely to ebb later due to uncertainty over the currency market," one trader said.
The dollar rebounded above 112 yen in Tokyo on Friday morning. Unless the dollar actually collapsed, the gold market would edge lower next week, Spall said.
A senior gold source said options-related delta hedging by producers was putting more significant pressure on the market.
"There are a lot of options being written by a few major producers," the senior trader said, noting the past week had been particularly marked by such activity.

"Because the gold price is where it is, there is a natural reluctance on behalf of producers to commit to selling gold when it could be cheaper tomorrow," he said. Instead of hedging by selling forward, producers were hedging by granting options.
Many traders saw the market well supported around $380, with strong physical demand in the Far East, Middle East and Turkey.
Physical gold demand in Asia had softened slightly after buyers snapped up the yellow metal when it slid below US$378 an ounce, Singapore and Hong Kong dealers said.
"There was good physical demand at $377," said a Hong Kong trader at a local bullion firm.
"Everybody bought on the dips and since they have bought all their needs, the people have stepped out of the market," a Singapore-based bank dealer said.
Most of the recent demand in Singapore was fuelled by Indian buyers making purchases ahead of the Diwali festival of lights this weekend, gold dealers said.
Prices would probably range between $378 and $382 an ounce, the traders added.
Singapore gold premiums were quoted in a range between 35-45 U.S. cents an ounce against 35-50 U.S. cents last week.
"Premiums have been stabilising. With demand slightly weaker, the premiums came off very, very slightly," another trader said.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6358, with a contribution from Rene Pastor in Singapore (65)870 3174
